title: Google reminds Android users of an overlooked scam detection tool
summary: Circle to Search and Google Lens can also help you detect scams!
body: TL;DR Google is highlighting Circle to Search’s existing ability to identify suspicious text messages using AI Overviews. We tested the functionality, and it works as intended, with Google explaining why a message might be fraudulent and suggesting next steps. Google Lens offers the same scam-checking functionality on phones without Circle to Search, including iPhones. Google’s suite of scam detection features is great at filtering out suspicious messages and calls before you fall for them. The tech giant has been steadily improving the collection and rolling it out to more users, though that’s also the big catch here. Not all scam detection features are available on every Android phone. Newer developments, like enhanced protection mode in Google Messages , are available on even fewer devices. With the company announcing new tools, it’s worth revisiting an existing one that’s available to a much wider range of users and devices. Google is highlighting that scam detection is available via Circle to Search (CtS) , giving a larger subset of users who don’t have scam detection natively access to preventive tools that can help them avoid falling victim to fraud.

title: Songwriter Streaming Royalties: Read What Every Streamer, Publisher & Songwriter Group Has Proposed
summary: From Spotify to the NMPA, the various stakeholders in the Copyright Royalty Board’s Phono V process have made their positions known.
body: The music industry’s latest battle over songwriter streaming royalties in the U.S. is currently underway, and streaming services, publishers and songwriters are now weighing in on what they think the royalty rate should be. The process, determined through the oversight of a government-sanctioned court called the Copyright Royalty Board (CRB), sets one of the royalty types (called “mechanicals”) songwriters earn on streaming services for a five-year period. Mechanicals make up roughly half of the money songwriters earn from streaming services. Given that the  U.S. is one of the biggest, most lucrative markets in the world, the rates that get set in America are hugely important to the well-being of songwriters and music publishers locally and even in far-flung areas of the world. title: ANBERNIC is quietly removing a controversial extra from its Android handhelds
summary: The company is dropping microSD card bundle options just days after facing accusations of distributing pirated games.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ANBERNIC has started removing optional microSD card bundles from several handheld listings on its official store. The changes follow an ESA complaint accusing ANBERNIC of selling devices bundled with unauthorized games. ANBERNIC hasn’t confirmed a connection, but the move may be intended to head off further action against the company. ANBERNIC has had quite a week. After recently unveiling its Nintendo 3DS-inspired RG DDS handheld — whose potential pricing was leaked earlier today — the company found itself facing scrutiny over the copyrighted games allegedly bundled with its devices. Within days of the complaint coming to light, ANBERNIC now appears to be quietly removing the contentious microSD card options from its online store. As spotted by Retro Handhelds , several ANBERNIC handheld listings have lost the option to purchase additional microSD cards alongside the devices. The publication compared an archived version of the RG SP listing from August 14 with the current storefront, finding that only the 16GB option remains. That card is still needed because it contains the handheld’s stock firmware.

summary: Samsung just got a free marketing boost.
body: TL;DR Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 series is seeing strong demand, exceeding the company’s initial sales expectations. Samsung says demand for its latest foldables is up 16% since launch, while Google searches for Samsung foldables have surged 300% over the past month. Apple’s entry into the foldable market with the iPhone Duo could be driving more consumers to explore Samsung’s alternatives. There’s no denying that Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 series is having its moment. The South Korean tech giant’s decision to split the book-style segment into two — regular and widescreen — seems to be paying off. We reported that despite an overall decline in global smartphone shipments, strong demand for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series has softened the blow for Samsung, and while the credit does go to Samsung for refining its lineup, there also appear to be some outside forces at play. Interestingly, one of those outside forces is Samsung’s biggest rival.

title: Is your Pixel recording unusually quiet audio? You’re not alone
summary: Still dealing with microphone issues first reported back in 2024.
body: TL;DR Several Pixel owners are reporting unusually low microphone volume when recording audio/video natively or via certain apps. Similar complaints date back to 2024 and span multiple Pixel generations, including the latest Pixel 10 series. Google appears to be aware of the complaints but hasn’t publicly acknowledged a widespread issue, and there’s no confirmed fix yet. Apart from offering one of the best software experiences in the Android smartphone ecosystem, Google’s Pixel line is also known for its impressive camera capabilities . However, what good is a high-res video recording if you can barely hear anything when you play it back? That’s exactly the frustration that a lot of Pixel owners are (and have been) dealing with. This isn’t a brand new issue, but it is resurfacing now. Reports about Pixel microphones recording audio that’s too quiet to hear can be traced back to 2024, and similar microphone problems appear to have continued to plague users since.

title: Google might soon borrow a sleeper Safari feature for Chrome
summary: Google is working on an effortless way to copy multiple links at once in Chrome.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is working on a button to copy multiple links at once. Engineers are exploring a button to copy URLs for all tabs in a group with a single click. The one who proposed it says the feature could allow users to easily copy multiple source links at once and share them with an AI chatbot. AI browsers have been cropping from the left, right, and center, and to keep up with intense competition, Google wants Chrome to feel as exciting as it did at launch . This is why Google is committing to delivering new Chrome features every two weeks , and one such feature could actually make researching and working with AI interfaces much easier. Google is testing a new menu option that lets you copy multiple links at once. Based on a Chromium-related thread on Google’s Issue Tracker (via Piunika Web ), Google engineers are exploring a single button to copy URLs for all tabs in a single tab group.

title: Samsung could have two more foldable surprises in 2027, for a total of six new foldables
summary: The next Galaxy Z lineup could include a phone that doesn't fold.
body: TL;DR A new leak claims Samsung’s 2027 Galaxy Z lineup could include six devices, including a Galaxy Z Fold 9 Pro and a Galaxy Z Slide. The tipster also claims improvements in battery, thickness, and weight across the lineup, with the TriFold 2 set to arrive first. Samsung has demonstrated slidable display technology, but the six-device lineup remains unverified, and earlier reporting points to a 2028 rollable launch. Samsung had barely unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold 8 family and Z Flip 8 when reports emerged suggesting its 2027 flagship lineup could grow to eight phones , including four foldables. That already sounded ambitious. Now, a fresh leak adds two more names to the Galaxy Z guest list, and one suggests Samsung’s next trick might involve less folding and more stretching. There are some notable glitches at this juncture, but performance is otherwise great on even budget Android devices. The port comes roughly two weeks after the Wii game was first decompiled. We saw a major milestone recently as Super Mario Galaxy became the first Wii game to be fully decompiled . This reverse-engineering milestone opens the door to fan ports of the game on other platforms, while also helping the community understand its inner workings. title: We asked how you feel about yearly smartphone launches, and the results are depressing
summary: Even Android enthusiasts are getting bored of annual smartphone launches.
body: We’re an enthusiast-first website, and that’s precisely why results from a recent poll we ran are particularly telling. There was a time when a new smartphone launch was genuinely something to look forward to. With an audience like ours — people who follow the smartphone industry closely — you’d expect excitement surrounding annual smartphone launches to be high. That doesn’t seem to be the case. We asked our readers how they feel about annual smartphone launches, and only 5% of respondents showed any meaningful excitement. The majority, on the other hand, said that they were starting to lose interest.

title: 5 One UI settings I always turn off on my Samsung Galaxy phone
summary: I never use a new Galaxy phone without making these changes.
body: My primary smartphone is an Android, and unless I’m testing a new device, I almost always use a Galaxy phone. I find One UI the best Android interface out there currently. It’s fast, customizable, and packed with several useful features that other Android skins don’t offer. That said, I can’t use One UI in its default settings: some aren’t configured to my preferences, while others are overly privacy-invasive and harvest data in the background. For this reason, I always disable numerous One UI settings on any Galaxy phone before I start using it. Here are some crucial ones you can consider turning off too.

title: Why my favorite 2026 smartwatch isn’t a Pixel Watch or Galaxy Watch
summary: Instead, it's the Amazfit Balance Ultra.
body: When we talk about smartwatches, especially Android-compatible ones, it’s easy to get laser-focused on Samsung and Google. The Pixel Watch has cemented itself as a showcase for Wear OS, while Galaxy Watches are the go-to choice if you have a Samsung phone. There’s nothing wrong with Google and Samsung’s wearables; the Pixel Watch 5 and Galaxy Watch 9 are both extremely good. But neither one is the 2026 smartwatch that’s impressed me the most.

title: Qualcomm’s lengthy legal battle with Arm nets it $2 (not a typo) in damages
summary: Two dollars today, potentially billions tomorrow.
body: TL;DR A Delaware jury has awarded Qualcomm $2 in damages in its legal fight with Arm. The jury sided with Qualcomm on two counts, and with Arm on five counts. The legal battle will now go to a US federal judge who will resolve several other issues. Qualcomm and Arm have been involved in a series of legal battles over several issues over the last couple of years. Since Qualcomm acquired Nuvia back in 2021, Arm has threatened to cancel Qualcomm’s architecture licensing agreement (ALA), and Qualcomm has filed lawsuits against Arm. According to a Reuters report, the verdict is finally in for Qualcomm’s latest lawsuit against Arm. The Delaware jury has sided with Qualcomm on two counts, awarding it damages amounting to $2. Yes, that’s not a typo.

title: Lemon is a new Switch emulator for Android that picks up where Yuzu left off
summary: The Lemon emulator for Android even offers a Lite version for those with weaker devices.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A new Nintendo Switch emulator called Lemon has recently been released on Android. The app is based on Yuzu and was originally made for Snapdragon-powered devices, but has since received Mali GPU support. Lemon offers features like easy data transfer from rival Switch emulators, frame generation, and per-game controller layouts. We’ve seen plenty of Nintendo Switch emulators on Android over the past few years, although Nintendo has cracked down on some of them via legal threats. Now, a new Switch emulator has arrived on Android. Lemon is a Nintendo Switch emulator for Android that’s based on the Yuzu emulator project. The app was first released last month and has been receiving a steady stream of updates since then.

title: Someone got Googlebook OS running on a Chromebook, and it’s surprisingly smooth
summary: An experimental install suggests existing Chromebooks may handle Google's new OS just fine.
body: TL;DR A Reddit user has successfully installed Googlebook OS on an ASUS Chromebook Plus, making this one of the first examples we’ve seen on existing Chromebook hardware. The experimental setup reportedly feels fast and smooth, sometimes even faster than ChromeOS, though Wi-Fi, audio, and Pixel integration are currently broken. Google has already confirmed that some newer Chromebooks will eventually support Googlebook OS, but it hasn’t provided a public rollout timeline. Googlebook OS has barely had time to unpack its bags, yet enthusiasts are already asking one of the most important questions about Google’s new laptop platform: Do we really need to spend $1,000 on a new Googlebook to use it? Google has already confirmed that many newer Chromebooks will eventually be able to migrate from ChromeOS to Googlebook OS , but it hasn’t said which consumer models qualify or when those upgrades will arrive. Someone has now decided not to wait. A Reddit user has successfully installed Googlebook OS on an ASUS Chromebook Plus, apparently making this one of the first examples we’ve seen of Google’s new operating system running directly on existing Chromebook hardware. And the early impression…

title: There’s okay news and bad news for Galaxy A58 cameras
summary: Update: The Galaxy A38 won't get camera hardware upgrades either, according to a trusted outlet.
body: Credit: Rushil Agrawal / Android Authority TL;DR A trusted source has revealed that the Samsung Galaxy A58 will retain the same cameras as the Galaxy A57. That means a 50MP main camera, a 12MP ultrawide camera, and a 5MP macro camera. This would be the eighth mainline Galaxy A50 series phone with a macro camera. Update: October 15, 2026 (7:20 AM ET): There’s also bad news if you were hoping that the Galaxy A38 5G would receive camera hardware upgrades. Galaxy Club reports that the upcoming phone will also feature a 50MP main camera, 12MP ultrawide camera, and 5MP macro lens. That’s the same camera setup as the Galaxy A37 and A36. Rounding out the package is a 12MP selfie camera. It’s possible that the Galaxy A38 5G could get other upgrades like a larger battery, improved screen, or faster processor. But smartphone photographers on a budget will likely be disappointed.

summary: Google's downplaying Spark branding in favor of a new 'Task' button.
body: TL;DR Gemini Spark now lives on the app’s home screen on mobile. Spark is accessible through a new button labeled Task. Chat and task history has also been reorganized. Gemini’s Spark feature that can automate your digital tasks is getting easier to access. A recent update adds a Task button to the Gemini app’s home screen, simplifying the process to set Gemini to work on all your mundane internet grunt work. title: Samsung Galaxy phones can’t tell if they’re connected to Bluetooth or not
summary: The Samsung Galaxy's volume slider is mixing up its connected device icons.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung Galaxy phone users are experiencing a strange bug affecting the volume panel. When playing audio through the phone’s speakers, a Bluetooth icon appears at the bottom of the slider. Instead of an earbud icon, a speaker icon reportedly appears when earbuds are connected. You may not always notice it, but the volume slider on your Galaxy phone conveys more information than just the volume level. Whether you’re listening to music through your earbuds or blasting it through your Bluetooth speakers, there will be a little symbol at the bottom of the panel that lets you know what your phone is connected to. However, a new bug is causing issues with this indicator. Samsung Galaxy phone users ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) are experiencing a strange glitch affecting the volume panel. When playing audio through the handset’s speakers, a Bluetooth icon appears at the bottom of the slider. That should not be happening, as it suggests the phone is connected to a Bluetooth device even though it is disconnected. Users also report seeing a speaker icon instead of an earbud icon when their earbuds are connected.

title: Pixel users report frustrating screen animation bugs after Android 17 QPR1 update
summary: The issue is primarily being reported by Pixel 10 users.
body: TL;DR September’s Android 17 QPR1 release has caused a problem for Pixel owners who are experiencing incorrect animations on the home and recent apps screens. The issue seems like it might be limited to the Pixel 10 series. Google is aware of the problem and is investigating it. For a phone that’s at the forefront of Android developments, the Pixel is also a leader when it comes to bugs. The latest has arrived with September’s Android 17 QPR1 release . Pixel owners are registering an issue they’re having with incorrect animations on the home and recent apps screens ever since the update. Over on Reddit’s Pixel sub, our original poster shares that when they try to return to the launcher from an app on their Pixel 10 Pro XL, instead of the downward animation they previously would get, the app goes to the recent apps screen and then slides away to the right. Additionally, they note that when they go to the recent apps screen from within an app, the app icon sometimes gets stuck on the screen while the recent apps screen opens behind it.

title: Survey reveals Kindle readers aren’t buying Amazon’s pricey page-turning solution
summary: Amazon's new Kindle Page-Turn Cover promises extra convenience, but our readers have strong opinions about the price tag.
body: Credit: Amazon Physical page-turn buttons might seem like a pretty basic feature for an e-reader , but Amazon has spent years leaving them off its Kindle lineup. The company has given bookworms a way to bring them back with its latest devices, although it’s charging a hefty premium for the privilege. We recently asked readers whether they’d be willing to pay $80 for this convenience, and the results suggest Amazon might have misread the room. As my colleague Dhruv Bhutani explained in his recent look at the 2026 Kindle refresh , Amazon’s new Page-Turn Cover adds physical buttons to the e-reader through a magnetic connection. The catch is that it costs $80 and it only works with the Signature Editions of the Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft, which already cost $250 and $320, respectively. That makes $330 the minimum entry price if you want physical buttons on a new Kindle. We wanted to know whether you thought this was fair enough, or if perhaps Amazon should have just included this functionality as part of the deal.

title: Samsung’s Good Lock team confirms widget text and volume slider bugs
summary: If you're also experiencing these problems, you can rest easy knowing Samsung is working on a fix.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Good Lock users are reporting a problem with text size when reducing the size of widgets and icons. Samsung states that it is searching for ways to solve the problem. The team has also confirmed a bug where different volume levels are displayed on the Quick Settings panel and the volume panel. One of the nice things about Galaxy phones is how customizable they can be. With the Good Lock app, you can modify almost your entire experience, from adding custom styles and animations to notifications to adjusting the layout and spacing of tiles in Quick Settings. However, as with any software, a bug can ruin the experience. Unfortunately, there are two bugs that are currently annoying Good Lock users. The first bug is connected to the Good Lock module known as Home Up. If you’re not familiar with Home Up, it allows you to reposition apps anywhere on the screen, resize widgets, and more. The problem in question deals with resizing widgets. As one user explains , when they reduce the size of icons and widgets, the text becomes proportional in size. The text can get so small that it becomes illegible.

Galaxy S27 season is creeping up: Samsung’s next non-folding flagships should be here in just a few months. We’ve already seen leaks about the phones’ hardware design , cameras , and other specs . Galaxy Club reports that, in contrast with the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra, the two lesser models will stick with the same front-facing camera as this year’s Galaxy S26 series. That’s a 12-megapixel shooter that’s been unchanged for several generations.

title: Your Android phone can now shut down or restart your PC
summary: Not around your PC to restart or shut it down? The Link to Windows app now lets you do it remotely.
body: TL;DR The Link to Windows app is getting new power control options, letting users remotely shut down, restart, or put their computer to sleep. These key functions were first revealed in a report last month and now appear to be rolling out through the latest Link to Windows beta. In addition to letting you control key power options, the new menu in the Link to Windows app also lets you finish updates before you restart or shut down the PC. Microsoft’s Link to Windows is a useful utility app that lets you remotely access certain phone functions on your Windows computer. It currently lets you access phone calls, messages, photos, and transfer files between your desktop and a linked Android phone. We recently learned that Microsoft is adding the ability to remotely shut down , restart, or put your computer to sleep . These functions are now officially rolling out in the Link to Windows app. While Link to Windows currently lets you lock your computer, the version 1.26101.103.0 beta adds additional controls for common actions.

title: Yikes: Google let a fake Chrome app on the Play Store, and it got over 100,000 downloads
summary: Sideloading is risky, but apparently so is the Play Store.
body: TL;DR A fake Google Chrome app with over 100,000 downloads was available on the Play Store. The app, from a developer named “Hizbartech,” even paid its way to the top of the search results for “Chrome.” Google has since removed the app, but it raises questions about the Play Store’s review and ad practices. Google talks a big game about trying to keep the Android ecosystem safe and secure. The company recently started cracking down on sideloading apps because malicious actors can easily create fake apps and trick users into installing them. Instead, Google wants users to install apps directly from the Play Store. The idea is that installing apps from the Play Store pretty much guarantees you won’t install a fake or malicious app. However, Google doesn’t seem to be doing a stellar job of keeping the Play Store safe, either.

title: Google is selling Pixel and Samsung phones inside the Play Store

Earlier this year, the company started showing banners for the Galaxy Watch 8 inside the Play Store . However, if you thought that was all Google would do, you were wrong. Google has quietly added a new “Shop devices” option in the Play Store’s account switcher (h/t Telegram user catat2am). The tip we originally received showed Samsung devices like the Galaxy S26 Ultra and the Galaxy S26 alongside Google devices.

title: PSA: Google is silently linking your phone number across all signed-in accounts
summary: Android’s phone number verification setting is opt-out, and links your number across every Google account on your device.
body: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Google now automatically verifies and attaches your phone number to every Google account signed in on your Android device without explicit prompts. Google updated its documentation between August and October 2025 to reflect this opt-out behavior, which links numbers across secondary, work, and alt profiles. Users can turn off “Verify phone numbers automatically” in their Android device’s Google settings page, but previously linked numbers must be manually removed from each Google account’s Personal Info page. Your Android phone is deeply integrated with a number of Google services, but a quiet background mechanism is currently causing a stir among users. A growing number of Android users are only now learning that Google automatically verifies and associates their phone number with every Google account logged into their device, without any explicit confirmation prompt. As spotted in a recent Reddit thread, users report receiving confirmation emails out of the blue from “noreply-phone-verification@google.com” stating that their phone number has been verified. The feature, known in Google settings as “Phone number verification,” links y…

title: The iPhone 18 Pro’s new camera feature is a sneaky trap for Android brands
summary: We've been here before.
body: One of the biggest talking points about the iPhone 18 Pro series is the mechanical variable-aperture lens on the primary rear camera. Apple is far from the first to market with this tech, but as we see time and again, Android brands will rush to copy this feature into upcoming flagships. In the interest of our collective wallets, Android OEMs should resist the knee-jerk impulse: without a substantially large imaging sensor to back it up, variable aperture adds unnecessary manufacturing costs and mechanical complexity for little real-world payoff.

title: I tried gaming on a Googlebook — here’s the good (and bad) news
summary: Intel-based Googlebooks are a clear step down from Snapdragon-powered models.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority We’ve waited a while, but the first Googlebooks are finally on the market. These laptops run on a so-called Googlebook OS platform, touted as a hybrid of Android and Chrome OS. The big draws of Googlebooks are features like deep Gemini integration, Android app support, and the ability to stream apps from your phone. Can you actually play games and emulators on Googlebooks, though? That was one of the first thoughts I had when I realized I’d be getting a review unit. So, I thought it would be a good idea to find out.

title: Samsung is expanding One UI 9 with Android 17 to the oldest qualifying flagships
summary: Just days after Galaxy S24, the Galaxy S23 is starting to receive stable One UI 9.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Stable One UI 9 has arrived for the Galaxy S23 series phones. The update is currently limited to users previously beta-testing One UI 9 on their Galaxy S23 in South Korea. Based on the rollout for other devices, the stable One UI 9 update for all users across different regions should be here in a week or two. Samsung started rolling out stable One UI 9 , based on Android 17, in late September. Over the past three or so weeks, several of Samsung’s older flagships — and even the latest Galaxy A series phone — have received the update. And now, it’s coming to even older devices. Based on a post in Samsung’s Community forums (via tipster Tarun Vats on X ), One UI 9 has seemingly started to roll out for Galaxy S23 users, just a couple of days after the Galaxy S24 series got its update in the US. The release is not available to all, but is currently limited to a smaller section of users who were previously beta testing One UI 9 on their Galaxy S23 devices. Furthermore, the release is currently limited to South Korea, Samsung’s home country.

title: Want to show an iPhone on TV? These are some of Apple’s ridiculous licensing rules
summary: We've known that bad guys can't use iPhones, but Apple's list of restrictions is really something.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR A Canadian TV show has reportedly switched from iPhones to Android phones due to Apple’s extensive list of requirements. Some of Apple’s demands include that no character can damage or destroy an iPhone, use a damaged model, or use an iPhone with a protective case. The production company is now mostly using Galaxy phones in lieu of iPhones. It’s not uncommon for TV shows and movies to use iPhones , but we’ve frequently heard that Apple doesn’t allow villains to be shown using its products. Now, a TV series has abandoned iPhones altogether in favor of Android devices due to Apple’s extensive list of rules. La Presse reports (via Mobile Syrup and iPhone in Canada ) that characters in Canadian series Antigang now use Android devices instead of iPhones. More specifically, the production is mostly using Samsung Galaxy phones .
